posts.author: ReadyForSeason
posts.paraphrase: Opening post. Asks whether people carry their laptop in a stylish, expensive tote or messenger bag, or in a backpack. Does not describe their own situation.
posts.quote: sassy expensive tote

posts.author: Midnight0
posts.paraphrase: Uses a backpack to keep hands free while hurrying around town; dislikes having things in hand or on the shoulder.
posts.quote: I hate having things in my hands or on my shoulder while rushing about town.

posts.author: Zebrasinpyjamas
posts.paraphrase: Uses a leather backpack.
posts.quote: Leather backpack here!

posts.author: PinkLadyLove
posts.paraphrase: Carries a pricey laptop handbag plus a second handbag; accepts that both are very heavy because they look beautiful.
posts.quote: Both are insufferablely heavy but absolutely beautiful.

posts.author: endlesscraziness
posts.paraphrase: Bought a treat bag after a promotion, but it does not fit their lunch, so they ended up using an old backpack (later linked a Sophia & Matt backpack).
posts.quote: However it doesn't fit my lunch so I've ended up using an old backpack

posts.author: Twoshoesnewshoes
posts.paraphrase: Also uses a leather backpack, from a Clarks outlet.
posts.quote: leather backpack too

posts.author: Att1cusPund
posts.paraphrase: Chose a sensible backpack with padded straps to ease shoulder strain; picked a Herschel.
posts.quote: Sensible backpack with padded straps.

posts.author: atomicnotsoblonde
posts.paraphrase: Uses a leather Osprey laptop handbag daily and loves it; clarified in a follow-up that it is a laptop handbag, not a tote.
posts.quote: I have a beautiful leather osprey handbag. I love it and use it daily

posts.author: Wednesday6
posts.paraphrase: Carries a tote bought from a local farm shop.
posts.quote: Tote from our local farm shop

posts.author: SylvieLaufeydottir
posts.paraphrase: Cycles to work with a commuter backpack. When using public transport, used a La Mansio bag worn as a backpack, valuing it as practical and good-looking.
posts.quote: which is both practical and beautiful

posts.author: Watchinghockey
posts.paraphrase: Uses a backpack.
posts.quote: Backpack.

posts.author: givethedoggerbone
posts.paraphrase: Uses a Kanken backpack; their small laptop in its sleeve fits in the back pocket alongside the seat pad.
posts.quote: My laptop is pretty small so even when it's in it's sleeve it fits in the back pocket

posts.author: TeachesOfPeaches
posts.paraphrase: Carries a leather Aspinal tote.
posts.quote: Leather aspinals tote

posts.author: Strawberryshortcake90
posts.paraphrase: Uses a Coach tote bought at Bicester Village for £129.
posts.quote: I only paid £129 for it at Bicester Village

posts.author: Mysteriousgirl2
posts.paraphrase: Has a 17-inch laptop and is struggling to find a suitable bag for it.
posts.quote: a whopper, I know

posts.author: Dipsomaniax
posts.paraphrase: Carries the laptop in the cheapest bag available and drives to work so nobody sees it. On minimum wage, so will not buy an expensive brand like Osprey.
posts.quote: I carry mine in the cheapest of cheap bags

posts.author: dudsville
posts.paraphrase: Uses a proper backpack for hands-free comfort and back health; it holds lunch and extra layers. Misses handbags but admits the backpack is the better option.
posts.quote: i can't deny this is the better option.

posts.author: tchotchke
posts.paraphrase: Is tempted by a bag on a site that currently has a discount code bringing it down to £156.20 including shipping.
posts.quote: They have a code on there atm that brings it down to £156.20.

posts.author: RockaLock
posts.paraphrase: Used a Knomo backpack that fitted an old, large laptop and all their other things comfortably.
posts.quote: I have a knomo backpack that fitted the laptop and all my other stuff comfortably.

posts.author: viewsoftheshard
posts.paraphrase: Owns a Whistles leather backpack but has grown to hate it; feels like a school kid and ridiculous with it when going out after work. Also misses having a desk.
posts.quote: I feel like a school kid, and if I go out after work I feel ridiculous with it.

posts.author: XmasPartyhat
posts.paraphrase: Keeps the laptop in a large handbag with everything else; only walks between the door and the car, so weight is not an issue.
posts.quote: Mine is in my massive handbag along with all my other tat.

posts.author: OracleofWurms
posts.paraphrase: Uses a cheap wheeled business trolley or tote on wheels, bought secondhand from a market stall or eBay; prefers it to backpacks.
posts.quote: A cheap business trolley or tote bag on wheels

posts.author: Wallywobbles
posts.paraphrase: Recommends a laptop backpack from niid as the best they have owned.
posts.quote: A fantastic laptop backpack from niid.

posts.author: Dynamoat
posts.paraphrase: Uses a padded shoulder backpack bought for about £25 from Amazon that has lasted three years; chose it to balance the weight because they walk a lot, but feels slow (like a tortoise) in central London.
posts.quote: However once I'm in central London I do feel a bit like a tortoise.

posts.author: MrsMoastyToasty
posts.paraphrase: Uses a backpack provided by their employer.
posts.quote: A backpack provided by my employer.

posts.author: IHaveNeverLivedintheCastle
posts.paraphrase: Swapped a work-issued bag and a heavy leather-and-tweed bag for a light, padded nylon Radley bag; rejected backpacks outright.
posts.quote: I couldn't bring myself to use a backpack.

posts.author: ginoohginoginelli
posts.paraphrase: Uses a Roka backpack for comfort, looks and plenty of space.
posts.quote: Roka backpack. V comfortable to carry, lovely to look at

posts.author: RaininSummer
posts.paraphrase: Carries a backpack.
posts.quote: Backpack

posts.author: Spaghettieis
posts.paraphrase: Chose a backpack because a tote gets too heavy with a laptop and water bottle; uses a Fjällräven Kånken with a dedicated laptop pocket.
posts.quote: A tote is too heavy with laptop, water bottle etc.

posts.author: fluffyteach
posts.paraphrase: Uses a Mia Tui Sydney backpack, which they find very roomy; dislikes shoulder bags because they always slide off.
posts.quote: I hate having bags balanced on my shoulders as they always fall off.

posts.author: SwedishEdith
posts.paraphrase: Bought a cheap Decathlon backpack, prioritising the lightest option they could find.
posts.quote: Cheap backpack from Decathlon. Wanted the lightest thing I could find.

posts.author: Parker231
posts.paraphrase: Also uses a backpack; finds it comfortable and roomy enough for notebooks, papers, headphones and a mouse.
posts.quote: Same here but have to confess it’s really comfortable

posts.author: grumpycow1
posts.paraphrase: Uses a Rains backpack.
posts.quote: Rains backpack

posts.author: Lantyslee
posts.paraphrase: Uses a Roka backpack, bought to fit a large laptop from a previous job, so it has plenty of room.
posts.quote: I bought it to fit a large laptop from my last job so there's plenty of room.

posts.author: Delphigirl
posts.paraphrase: Carries a Knomo Hanover slim laptop briefcase by hand or messenger-style; likes its red lining. It fits a thin MacBook Air, an A4 notebook and papers, though the gusset is a bit tight.
posts.quote: which is very nice and has a sassy red lining

posts.author: Delphigirl
posts.paraphrase: Says they have never been able to use backpacks and apologises for it.
posts.quote: I can't do backpacks. I never have been able to. I'm not 15.

posts.author: givethedoggerbone
posts.paraphrase: Asks Delphigirl why they apologised.
posts.quote: Why have you apologised?

posts.author: Delphigirl
posts.paraphrase: Explains that backpacks are practical and popular but look childish to them; says it is personal taste, not meant as an insult.
posts.quote: they just seem childish to me. Personal taste, not trying to be insulting

posts.author: elizzza
posts.paraphrase: Uses a black Herschel backpack. Walks to work, drops off two children on the way and deals with frequent rain, so needs a hands-free bag and wants a waterproof hooded coat option; misses the camel coat and leather handbag of earlier work days.
posts.quote: Sadly my days of style over practicality are behind me.

posts.author: Reugny
posts.paraphrase: Owns two outdoor-shop backpacks including an Osprey, but mainly uses a light laptop bag bought from Amazon. Sometimes carries two laptops on public transport, where sleeves and backpacks help.
posts.quote: I mainly use a laptop bag. I brought the bag of Amazon and it is light.

posts.author: wideawakeinthemiddleofthenightagain
posts.paraphrase: Drives to the office with a leather laptop tote and a handbag. On London train commutes switches between a rucksack, a convertible leather bag and the tote depending on footwear, weather, evening plans and how they want to be perceived; heels plus tote plus lots of walking is miserable.
posts.quote: high heels plus tote bag plus lots of walking makes me want to cry!

posts.author: Yogaandchocolate
posts.paraphrase: Carries a Coach leather tote. After an occupational health questionnaire asked how they carry their laptop, they now get regular emails saying the bag is non-compliant with OH policy, which they ignore.
posts.quote: As a result I’m now getting regular emails about my bag being non compliant with OH policy

posts.author: JustGotToKeepOnKeepingOn
posts.paraphrase: Dislikes backpacks on public transport (awkward to take off, pickpocket worries, bumping people's faces) and thinks they look poor on them. Uses an across-body laptop bag plus a handbag and wants an affordable handbag-style laptop bag.
posts.quote: There is a huge gap in the market for a decent handbag to carry a laptop that doesn't cost a fortune.

posts.author: VitoCorleoneOfMNMafia
posts.paraphrase: Sarcastically remarks that the employer hopefully paid for the laptop, admitting they are missing the point of the thread.
posts.quote: Hopefully your employer paid for that laptop.

posts.author: Delphigirl
posts.paraphrase: Has largely stopped carrying a handbag when carrying a work bag; pays with Apple Pay, so the laptop bag holds just phone, security cards, lipstick and pens.
posts.quote: I have pretty much ditched a handbag if I have to carry a work bag.

posts.author: VitoCorleoneOfMNMafia
posts.paraphrase: Uses a rucksack with a waist belt to take weight off the shoulders while carrying other equipment.
posts.quote: I use a rucksack with a waist belt to take the weight off my shoulders

posts.author: BlowingAway
posts.paraphrase: Uses a leather backpack that converts into a handbag (linked an ISMAD Cleo 2-in-1 backpack) and finds it clever.
posts.quote: I have a leather backpack which also transforms into a handbag. Clever.

posts.author: flowerchild2000
posts.paraphrase: Carries a very expensive custom-built laptop in a flimsy old canvas backpack, admits it looks teenage, and plans to replace it.
posts.quote: I have a very expensive custom built laptop that I carry in a flimsy old canvas backpack

posts.author: StarlightLady
posts.paraphrase: Uses a shabby backpack deliberately so it does not attract muggers.
posts.quote: A tatty back pack that does not scream “mug me”!

posts.author: featheryfancy
posts.paraphrase: Carries a Cambridge Satchel Co leather bag bought in a Boxing Day sale a few years ago.
posts.quote: Got it in the Boxing Day sale a few years ago

posts.author: Spaghettieis
posts.paraphrase: Used a tote for school at 15 in an impractical teenage way; as an adult now uses a backpack.
posts.quote: in the classic impractical way of the teenager

posts.author: Darhon
posts.paraphrase: Uses a backpack because they carry lots of other gear, take the train and walk between sites; would not use one if they drove and stayed in one place.
posts.quote: it's just the best option

posts.author: BiblicallyAccurateAngel
posts.paraphrase: Uses a backpack because of a long walk on their commute.
posts.quote: Backpack due to long walk on my commute.

posts.author: TheDandyLion
posts.paraphrase: Still uses an Eastpak backpack from secondary school, testing its 25-year guarantee; admits it is not stylish and wants a new one.
posts.quote: I'm testing its 25yr guarentee.

posts.author: SaltyGod
posts.paraphrase: Uses a leather tote because the commute is mostly by car and the laptop is not heavy.
posts.quote: as my commute is mostly in the car and laptop isn’t heavy

posts.author: CattingAbout
posts.paraphrase: Uses a laptop backpack that also holds lunch; not the smartest or smallest, but better-looking than juggling two or three bags.
posts.quote: everything fits in it, so still looks better than carrying 2-3 different things!

posts.author: MaryMcI
posts.paraphrase: Was given a work laptop with no bag, so uses their child's old school bag for now and plans to buy a proper one later.
posts.quote: We were provided laptops, but nothing to carry them in.

posts.author: BiblicallyAccurateAngel
posts.paraphrase: Says the standard laptop bags their employer provided signal that the carrier has a laptop and invite muggers.
posts.quote: We were given standard laptop bags, which scream "I've got a laptop, mug me!".

posts.author: GreatGateauxsby
posts.paraphrase: Uses a backpack for work and keeps handbags for weekends and special occasions, not wanting expensive bags damaged; mentions Dior's £1 shopper as proof sturdy bags can carry a ThinkPad.
posts.quote: i have too many expensive ones and don’t want them trashed

posts.author: dgirluk
posts.paraphrase: Wants a comfortable, roomy backpack with padded straps and a back that does not get sweaty, and asks for recommendations. Takes the backpack off on trains/tube to avoid bumping people and carries a small shoulder bag for phone, ID and essentials.
posts.quote: I always take it off when I get on the train/tube because I don't want to mistakenly bash anybody

posts.author: JesusMaryAndJosephAndTheWeeDon
posts.paraphrase: Backpacks hurt their neck, so they swapped a hiking rucksack for a bum bag. Their work cross-body bag has a broken zip and work would only offer a backpack instead; asks for recommendations.
posts.quote: They also hurt my neck to the extent I swapped my hiking rucksack for a hiking bum bag.

posts.author: VelvetVoice
posts.paraphrase: Still searching for a work backpack; would like a nice tote but finds it impractical on public transport and rainy days. Uses a black Kipling bought for their child in Year 6 and feels awkward using it.
posts.quote: it is not practical on public transport and rainy days

posts.author: RosesAndHellebores
posts.paraphrase: Uses an old TK Maxx backpack for laptop, notepad and papers while moving between home, car, office and buildings on a large site; hopes it lasts until they retire in 21 months.
posts.quote: Hoping it lasts another 21 months until I retire.

posts.author: greenacrylicpaint
posts.paraphrase: Uses a laptop backpack because the laptop is too heavy to carry on one shoulder for more than a few minutes.
posts.quote: just too heavy to carry over shoulder for more than a few minutes.

posts.author: nutsnutspistachionuts
posts.paraphrase: Uses a Sandqvist Hege backpack that holds a small work laptop, a MacBook Air, spare clothes, a wash bag, notebooks and both chargers; hates carrying that load but says the bag can.
posts.quote: I hate carrying all that, but it can.

posts.author: horseymum
posts.paraphrase: Recommends a backpack and warns not to damage neck and shoulders just because another bag looks better.
posts.quote: don't damage your neck/ shoulders because something looks better.

posts.author: Pinko1
posts.paraphrase: Moved from a fancy baby changing bag to a neoprene-style backpack, which they think looks great; feels backpacks look less dated now, though colleagues use canvas ones.
posts.quote: Upgraded to a neoprene style backpack and it looks amazing now.

posts.author: InSpainTheRain
posts.paraphrase: Uses a Tumi Voyageur Benin 15.6-inch laptop case from John Lewis and loves it.
posts.quote: I use this and I love it.

posts.author: Faceplantagain
posts.paraphrase: Uses a leather backpack (possibly from John Lewis's men's range) plus a small cross-body bag for phone and debit card so they do not have to dig in the backpack while commuting.
posts.quote: so I don't have to be getting stuff in and out of the backpack when commuting.

posts.author: WingBingo
posts.paraphrase: Uses a Dr Martens backpack, finding it hard-wearing, functional and a bit stylish.
posts.quote: Hard wearing, functional and a bit stylish.

posts.author: Orcadianrythyms
posts.paraphrase: Uses a Naledi Copenhagen Alex bag, a tote that converts to crossbody; it holds a laptop, notepads and handbag items, with a liner to prevent lipstick or pen damage, and looks almost new after daily use.
posts.quote: It’s amazing quality and has been in daily use

posts.author: HeadNorth
posts.paraphrase: Uses a medium Roka backpack in Barbie pink for train and walking commutes; thinks backpacks are more practical than totes and says most commuters they see use one.
posts.quote: I think form should follow function.

posts.author: Purplecatshopaholic
posts.paraphrase: Employer provided a backpack, but they bought a wheeled trolley case because of a bad back; it fits everything with no strain.
posts.quote: I invested in a trolley case with wheels as I have a bad back.
